What Needs You, on Home, holds the questions you need to answer and the notices that tell you what happened. A question has its answers as buttons, such as File It or Keep The Account, and Dismiss. A notice says what happened: groceries you couldn’t pay for, a commitment you slept through, a welcome to the school. The number beside Home on the menu counts both.

Where To Find It
Home, The What Needs You Panel.
When You Can Use It
From “What Needs You”.
Show Me Where
What To Press
Open Home and read What Needs You: questions first, then notices.
Press one of a question’s answers to act on it from What Needs You, without opening its screen. An answer does what the same action does on the question’s own screen: File It, on your tax return’s question, files the return just as File It on Papers does.
Press Go There to open the screen a question or a notice is about.
Press Dismiss to take a question off the list without answering it.
Press Mark N Read, at the top of the panel, to mark every unread notice read at once.
Press Show All N, under the notices, to see every unread one before you do: the panel draws the six most important first, and Show The Six Most Important goes back to them.
Press a question’s or a notice’s title to open it: how urgent or important it is, when it closes, and where it sits in the list.

DRAM 103a/b · Due September 21, 2026 · Skills: Scene Study, Character Work, Emotional Depth

How This Works
Riders to the Sea, J. M. Synge (1904), the kitchen of a cottage on an island off the west of Ireland: you play Nora, Elena Kim plays Cathleen. While their mother sleeps, Nora brings in a bundle the young priest gave her: a shirt and a plain stocking taken off a drowned man in Donegal. Their brother Michael has been lost at sea, and their other brother Bartley means to sail to the horse fair at Galway. The sisters hide the bundle from their mother; later, alone, they open it and know the stocking by Nora’s own stitches.

No Claim Open
How This Works

Connecticut treats a full-time student as not available for work (CGS 31-235(b)), so a claim pays only once you’ve left school.

Once a claim is open, the game certifies each week for you on Sunday, from anywhere in the country, as an interstate claim allows. What it pays is taxable income on your return.

A week with work pays the benefit less two-thirds of the pay, counting the work you did that week, even if it’s paid later. A week pays nothing if you’re abroad, a full-time student in Connecticut or without permission to work in the US, or in hospital or laid up by an injury for most of the week. Work-study wages come from your school and don’t count toward a claim’s base period.

Form I-765, (c)(3)(B), after your degree

How This Works

OPT is permission to work in your field after your degree, and it keeps your US status going. The game has no work after the degree, so an approved OPT ends after 90 days without work, about 90 days from its start, and your US status ends with it.
